column1: # The schedulers binaries/scx builds and carries (source of truth for the scheduler list), one per line, tab separated:  name <TAB> minimum kernel <TAB> description
# Adding one is a one-line change here (build.sh adds -p <name>, installs target/release/<name> as bin/<name>, copies the
# LICENSE of its directory under scheds/, runs <name> --version and lists it in the image's /schedulers.tsv).
#   name            the cargo package of the scheduler (a directory under scheds/rust or scheds/experimental of the scx source)
#   minimum kernel  MAJOR.MINOR, ONLY where the scheduler's README at the pinned tag states a minimum kernel; otherwise empty
#                   (scx_p2dq's README names 6.12 only for its optional --atq-enabled flag, so that is not a minimum)
#   description     one line of about 100 characters taken from the scheduler's README overview, no claims of our own
# Check the READMEs again when the pin in upstream.env is bumped. Rust schedulers: scx_beerland scx_bpfland scx_cake scx_chaos
# scx_cosmos scx_eevdf scx_flash scx_forge scx_lavd scx_layered scx_mitosis scx_p2dq scx_pandemonium scx_rusty (scheds/rust);
# scx_flow scx_mavd scx_mlfq scx_nitosis scx_rburst scx_reevdf scx_rlfifo scx_rlocal scx_rustland scx_rvtime scx_tickless
# (scheds/experimental). There is no scheds/c any more: the C example schedulers now live only in the Linux kernel tree
